newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha edges lower but Skikda closes again.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha edges lower but Skikda closes again.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices edged lower on Tuesday after Monday's late selloff in crude and a bit of follow through weakness today, traders said.

Naphtha also corrected some of last week's gains on signs the heavy buying interest into the United States, which apparently drew 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes out of Europe last week, was cooling off for the time being.
But Algeria's Skikda port closed again on Tuesday and signs the arbitrage to the U.S. remained attractive continued to underpin the market, they said.
Dec swaps fell $3 to $221.50/$222.50 to catch up to the late crude drop yesterday. Jan swaps held at a $8.50 backwardation, at $213/$214, and Feb fell $4.50 from Monday to trade at $205/$206.
Cargoes were notionally priced down $3 at $223/$226 cif.
"There is still going to be interest (to the States) as long as LPG prices stay high," said one trader.

At least one and maybe two other large cargoes of 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes were believed to be waiting for loading at Skikda, where bad weather closed the port for tanker loadings, according to shipping sources.

"I would say the market is fairly well balanced and we're getting a lot of offers for FOB material," in NWE, said one trader. "There is enough material around. If Skikda is closed again, there is no worry for buyers."
He said there were rumours that one, possibly two, large cargoes were being pieced together for loading in early December out of Skikda.
It was unclear, however, if the cargoes of 55,000-60,000 tonnes would end up in Europe or head to the United States because of the arbitrage, he said.
There are two smaller Russian cargoes reaching NWE this week and another likely to arrive early next week, he said.
